text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A member of opposition FORD-Asili party says the current crisis in the party is the fault of its chairman Kenneth Matiba.
- At least 70 people have died of cholera in the past week in Lokichogio town and Kakuma refugee camp in North Eastern Kenya.
- A top level delegation from Amnesty International will arrive next week to launch a Human Rights manifesto for Kenya.

- 24 parliamentarians from the Abaluhyia community warn that any physical harm inflicted on the FORD-Asili secretary general Martin Shikuku will be met with appropriate retaliation from the entire Luhya community.
- Nairobi City Council cancels the distribution of 14 plots of land that were irregularly allocated.
- Trade Unions in Kenya want constitutional talks after the general elections.
- The Computer Society of Kenya says it is not possible to rig elections with a computerised system of voter registration.
- A 19-year old man dismembers a one-month old baby and chops off his wife's arms with an axe following a bitter quarrel over the paternity of the child.
- The National Convention Executive Council now calls for a boycott of the ongoing voter registration exercise.
